- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 15–30% for short-term (1–7 day) horizons.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast lows by 10–25% for medium-term (8–21 day) horizons.
- Model consistently overreacts to sentiment spikes: if sentiment jumps >0.67 within 3 days, forecast should be capped at 1.2x historical mean for next 7 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion: if 18-day history shows volatility, forecast should be adjusted downward by 10–20% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Overshoot after spikes (e.g., 20+ day forecast > 5x historical max) should be clipped to 3x historical max unless sentiment confirms sustained bullish trend.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings, model tends to lag; add 0.1–0.3 to forecast for 1–3 day horizons to account for sentiment momentum.
